_what: Real discovery photographs for the tracking exhibit, from Wikimedia Commons via scripts/fetch_tracking_images.py. Credits were read from the Commons API.

images.caption: Clyde Tombaugh's two plates, 23 and 29 January 1930, Lowell Observatory. Pluto is the dot that moved (arrowed).
Sedna's discovery frames, 14 November 2003, Samuel Oschin Telescope, Palomar: three exposures over three hours.
2015 BP519 (circled) on 17 January 2015, the Dark Energy Survey's camera. A survey built for cosmology found one of the most extreme orbits known.
images.credit: Original images taken by Kathy Vivas, David Gerdes, Friedman/Dark Energy Survey/NOIRLab, processing and color compositing by Nrco0e
